title: Other genetic and congenital kidney disorders

steps.tx: Classic **X-linked Alport syndrome** is caused by pathogenic mutations in **COL4A5** on the X chromosome, accounting for approximately **85%** of all Alport pedigrees. Disruption of alpha-5(IV) collagen chain synthesis prevents normal assembly of the **alpha3.alpha4.alpha5(IV)** heterotrimer, leading to progressive sensorineural hearing loss, ocular lenticonus, and renal failure in hemizygous males.

vis.alt: Alport syndrome with basket-weave basement membrane, lenticonus, and cochlea
vis.caption: Basket-weave splitting of the glomerular basement membrane, anterior lenticonus, and the cochlea in Alport syndrome (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Ultrastructural examination of the glomerular basement membrane by transmission electron microscopy establishes the definitive hallmark of Alport syndrome: irregular alternating areas of thinning and marked thickening with a pathognomonic **basket-weave splitting** and lamellation of the **lamina densa**. This structural disruption contrasts sharply with uniform diffuse thinning seen in benign thin basement membrane nephropathy.

right.title: Thin Basement Membrane Disease

steps.tx: X-linked **Fabry disease** is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient activity of **alpha-galactosidase A** (**GLA** gene), causing progressive lysosomal accumulation of **globotriaosylceramide** (**Gb3**). Multiorgan manifestations encompass burning acroparesthesias, **angiokeratomas**, hypohidrosis, left ventricular hypertrophy, and vacuolated podocytes packed with pathognomonic zebra bodies on electron microscopy.

left.title: Fabry Disease Manifestations

steps.tx: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (**ADTKD**) is characterized by bland urinary sediment, slowly progressive chronic kidney disease, and autosomal dominant inheritance without significant proteinuria. The most common subtype is **ADTKD-UMOD**, caused by heterozygous mutations in the **uromodulin** gene, typically presenting with early-onset severe **hyperuricemia** and juvenile **gout**.

vis.alt: ADTKD-UMOD management: CKD care, RRT, transplantation, and cascade genetic testing
vis.caption: ADTKD-UMOD care moves from slowing chronic kidney disease to replacement therapy and family testing (StewardMD).

steps.tx: A second major subtype, **ADTKD-MUC1**, is caused by a unique cytosine insertion within a GC-rich variable number tandem repeat (**VNTR**) domain of the **mucin-1** gene. This frameshift generates a toxic mutant frameshift protein (**MUC1-fs**) that accumulates within the endoplasmic reticulum of tubular epithelial cells, necessitating specialized mass spectrometry or targeted sequencing.

steps.tx: Severe **Cystinosis** is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disease caused by mutations in **CTNS** (encoding **cystinosin**), leading to intralysosomal cystine crystal precipitation. Infantile nephropathic cystinosis represents the most frequent cause of inherited **renal Fanconi syndrome**, presenting with severe proximal tubular wasting, rickets, growth retardation, and diagnostic pathognomonic **corneal cystine crystals**.

left.title: Infantile Nephropathic Cystinosis
points: Treated with oral and topical cysteamine

right.title: Classic Cystinuria
points: Treated with urine alkalinization and tiopronin

steps.tx: The multi-organ ciliopathy **Bardet-Biedl syndrome** is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in **BBS genes** encoding the **BBSome** complex required for primary ciliary trafficking. Diagnostic clinical criteria comprise rod-cone **retinal dystrophy**, postaxial polydactyly, central obesity, hypogonadism, developmental delay, and structural renal dysmorphism with calyceal cysts.

steps.tx: Heterozygous mutations in the transcription factor **HNF1B** cause the autosomal dominant syndrome of **renal cysts and diabetes** (**RCAD**). Renal involvement features hyperechogenic enlarged kidneys, multiple bilateral cortical cysts, and congenital hypoplastic kidneys, associated with mature-onset diabetes of the young (**MODY5**), severe hypomagnesemia, and asymptomatic hyperuricemia.

steps.tx: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (**ARPKD**) is caused by biallelic mutations in **PKHD1** on chromosome 6p12, which encodes **fibrocystin**. Both kidneys are symmetrically enlarged and echogenic from fusiform collecting-duct ectasia. **Congenital hepatic fibrosis** is the liver half of the same ductal-plate defect, and portal hypertension can appear while kidney function is still preserved.
steps.say: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease is caused by mutations in PKHD1 on chromosome 6p12. The missing protein is fibrocystin, the collecting ducts dilate, and both kidneys enlarge. Congenital hepatic fibrosis is the liver half of the same defect, so portal hypertension can appear while kidney function is still preserved.

rows: Both kidneys enlarge, with fusiform collecting-duct ectasia
Congenital hepatic fibrosis and later portal hypertension
